title: SparkLend calibrates Slope 2 by asset class, at 300% for volatile collateral against 15% for stablecoins
content:
Slope 2 — the borrow rate at 100% utilization — is set in two distinct bands across the Ethereum deployment. Every dollar-pegged market sits at 15%: USDS, USDT, USDC, pyUSD, Dai (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.2.1.3, .1.5, .1.9, .1.18, and Dai in the preceding chunk). Volatile collateral sits an order of magnitude higher: WBTC, weETH, rETH, LBTC, tBTC, ezETH, rsETH, cbBTC and sUSDS all at 300%, wstETH at 200%, WETH at 75%.

The banding does not track credit risk — sUSDS and cbBTC are among the better-collateralized assets here and both sit at 300%. It tracks **exit urgency**. Slope 2 is the rate that only bites when the pool is fully lent out and no supplier can withdraw. The question it answers is: how bad is it if withdrawals are blocked in this asset for a day?

For a stablecoin, moderately bad and recoverable — the asset is not moving, and 15% is enough to pull repayment without punishing normal peak usage. For volatile collateral, potentially catastrophic: a supplier locked out of wstETH during a 20% drawdown loses far more to the price than to any rate, so the curve must make full utilization effectively unreachable rather than merely expensive. A 300% annualized rate does that.

The corollary is that Slope 2 is a liquidity-insurance premium priced in the asset's own volatility, and the two-band structure means SparkLend is making an asset-class judgment, not a per-asset one — the same simplification visible in the kill switch's uniform 0.95 thresholds.
description: The penalty rate at full utilization tracks how urgently suppliers may need to exit an asset, not its credit quality — stables cluster at 15%, crypto collateral at 100–300%.
